heading: Helix fits how you already work
description: Whether you're shipping solo or leading a team, Helix decomposes every prompt into small, reviewable units so you stay in control of the diff.

items.title: Solo Founders
items.description: Turn one big idea into a stack of small, reviewable PRs you can actually trust.
painPoints: AI generates a wall of code you can't review
Every change risks breaking the rest of the app
Hard to stay in flow when the diff is overwhelming
outcomes: Small, atomic PRs you can read in minutes
Stay in shipping mode instead of cleanup mode

items.title: Staff Engineers
items.tagline: Keep architectural standards as agents ship
items.description: Decomposition exposes intent; verification enforces the bar your codebase already expects.
painPoints: Agents bypass the conventions you spent years enforcing
Sprawling diffs hide subtle coupling and dead code
Review burden falls back on you either way
outcomes: Each unit is checked against types, tests, and lint

items.title: Engineering Managers
items.description: Helix turns agent output into a stream of safe, auditable work — your team reviews outcomes, not chaos.
painPoints: Throughput claims don't match what actually ships
Hard to attribute agent output to a deliverable
Quality drift erodes trust in the AI toolchain
outcomes: Each run is replayable and auditable end-to-end
Throughput measured in merged PRs, not tokens
Quality bar enforced automatically, not negotiated

items.title: Tech Leads
items.tagline: Stay close to the design without doing every PR
items.description: Dependency-aware execution keeps architectural seams intact so you can delegate safely.
painPoints: Agents love to refactor the wrong abstraction
Cross-cutting changes get committed in one shot
Hard to coach a team when the diff is unreadable
outcomes: Each PR is scoped to one architectural concern
Coach on the diff, not the cleanup

items.title: AI Engineers
items.tagline: A real orchestration substrate for agents
items.description: Helix is the runtime you wanted: explicit dependency graphs, repo-aware checks, replayable runs.
painPoints: Most 'agents' are prompts dressed up as systems
No notion of dependency between steps
Evaluation is an afterthought, not a primitive
outcomes: Explicit DAG with gated, parallel execution
Repo-aware verification as a first-class step
Replayable runs you can diff and audit
